text.p: The managing director of engineering firm Australian National Industries Ltd, Peter Stancliffe, said on Monday he would issue a statement this week about the boardroom dispute over the company's troubled investment in the Holter environmental operation.
"I think it is only fair that I do make my position known," Stancliffe told Reuters.

"In fact what you will find is when I do make my position known I won't be on one side or the other," he said in reference to the dispute involving two independent directors who have lost their power to investigate the Holter purchase by ANI in 1991.

Stancliffe said he had been overseas for three weeks and only returned on Sunday, missing the unauthorised statement issued by ANI independent directors Ross Palmer and Fred Smith and followed the next day by a highly critical ANI statement.
Palmer and Smith said they comprised a sub-committee of the board which was investigating the Holter purchase.

ANI chairman Ted Harris said on Monday that the powers of this committee had been revoked and a majority of the board had resolved to have the Holter inquiries undertaken by corporate barrister Bob Ellicott, QC. Harris also said he hoped for an end to negative speculation about the company.
